sentences.text: Xilousuchus was likely a large animal, estimated to be between three and four meters in length, possessing a small head and a sail-like structure running along its neck and back.

The preserved skull is fragmentary but includes much of the snout and maxilla, featuring a single tooth nearly 15 mm long with small serrations and backward curves that suggest it could puncture flesh or slice chunks of food.
Large, flattened neural spines on the cervical vertebrae formed this sail-like structure, with spine height increasing from 42 mm at the axis vertebra to 92 mm at the tenth cervical vertebra.
Xilousuchus is currently considered the oldest known archosaur, though it may be slightly younger than Ctenosauriscus and Vytshegdosuchus by less than one million years.
The presence of replacement teeth indicates that Xilousuchus was a polyphyodont, an animal that continuously replaces its teeth throughout its life.
Xilousuchus lived during the Lower Triassic (Olenekian stage) in northeastern Shanxi Province, China, with fossils found in the Heshanggou Formation of the Ordos Basin.
Xilousuchus was first described by Xiao-Chun Wu in 1981, with the type species named Xilousuchus sapingensis.
Xilousuchus likely had long, powerful legs and was probably an active hunter.
Research by Sterling J. Nesbitt in 2011 classified Xilousuchus as a poposauroid most closely related to Arizonasaurus, and it belongs to the family Ctenosauriscidae.
